evidence: Independent generator-only replay matched all stored invariants for all 1386 census rows.
Independent semigroup-tree enumeration through genus 12 produced counts 1,1,2,4,7,12,23,39,67,118,204,343,592; genus 6-12 generator sets matched the census exactly.
All 63 (g,m) stratum sizes, max-type values, min-Wilf values, and stored extremal witnesses independently recomputed with zero mismatches.
W=0 counts 6,3,4,5,6,2,9 and unique max type t=g in genera 6-12 independently confirmed.
Delgado-Eliahou-Fromentin (2025) already subsumes the boolean W>=0 claim by verifying Wilf through genus 100.
OEIS A007323 already records per-genus counts; OEIS A199711 already records counts by genus and multiplicity.
Standard software already computes the individual numerical-semigroup invariants, and the max-type values are not treated as the novelty basis.

The compared substantive sources do not provide the record's integrated per-semigroup genus-6-12 corpus plus exact minimum-Wilf values and named witnesses for every (g,m) stratum; originality is limited to that data/certificate layer.
The complete generator-indexed corpus is a reusable regression/benchmark data set for semigroup enumeration and invariant implementations.
Exact minimum-Wilf values and witnesses across all 63 strata provide concrete small-genus boundary cases.
Value is modest and computational: no new general Wilf theorem or improved verification range is claimed.

sources.title: A verification of Wilf's conjecture up to genus 100
An upper bound for the type of a numerical semigroup, and a reduction of Wilf's conjecture

limitations: Finite machine certificate, not formal verification.
Originality is limited to the integrated corpus and stratified minimum-Wilf witness data; several headline subclaims are known prior results.
